pull_requests.title: Harden supersession authority and add multi-domain retrieval evaluations
pull_requests.body:
An invalid successor could retire a valid predecessor because the reader trusted supersedes before checking integrity. Implicit retirement now requires intact records, unique IDs, correct hash pins, valid acyclic dependencies, and lineage-consistent depth. Valid retired successors preserve retirement history; explicit withdrawals remain retired.

Adds standard-library BM25 and TF-IDF baselines to the existing pottery kill tests, comparing stripped prose with the current page pool under the reader's depth limit. Includes per-probe predictions and reproducible saved comparisons without replacing historical results.

Adds 36 frozen synthetic developer-authored probes across software operations, library services, and office procedures. The runner validates probe hashes and label evidence, records corpus hashes, and reports per-domain/per-outcome results, return precision, and coverage. These fixtures are explicitly not independent validation. evaluation/README.md provides the protocol for separately authored questions, blinded human labels, adjudication, and an external audit; that human evaluation remains pending.

Validation: 122 combined tests, 52 smart-local tests, 145 swarm tests, 61 networked tests, and 93 image tests passed (473 total). All five example-site adoption checks passed with zero errors, and the local-mirror validator exited 0. Python compilation passed. Frozen multi-domain results and all three pottery baseline comparisons reproduce.

Compatibility: legacy unpinned references no longer retire predecessors implicitly until seal pins them. Other serving rules and historical benchmark files remain unchanged.

Add offline response smoke coverage for polite phrasing, whitespace, capitalization, curly apostrophes, misspellings, other subjects, missing facts, comparisons, conditions, negation, quoted commands, invalid input, tampered pages, and excluded attributes. Unsupported misspellings still decline safely; this change does not add fuzzy subject matching.

Validation: the existing suite passed 533 tests; the new smoke suite passed 4 tests. Focused reruns passed 13 grounded-chat tests, 3 question-frame tests, 29 provenance-gate tests, and 8 natural-guidance tests. git diff --check passed.

These are deterministic local synthetic checks, not independent evaluation or a guarantee for all possible phrasing.

pull_requests.title: Offer confirmed typo recovery while preserving source boundaries
pull_requests.body:
The 1,000-response development audit found that every tested misspelling safely refused but none helped the user recover.

Add a closed spelling-suggestion grammar for pronoun attribute questions. The reply asks the user to choose or resend a corrected question, names the selected topic explicitly, and supplies no evidence or automatic answer. Resubmitted questions use the unchanged provenance and evidence checks. Bare yes does not execute an old suggestion. Names, numbers, negation, quotations, comparisons, and conditions are not fuzzy-corrected.

Add regression coverage for confirmations, original transcripts, reloads, topic switches, stale suggestions, missing/conflicting facts, duplicate titles, altered/withdrawn/revised pages, delivery profiles, excluded attributes, and browser automatic lookup. Add the reproducible 1,000-question evaluator and compact results with source-file hashes.

Validation:
- Full regression suite: 544 tests passed.
- Final focused spelling suite: 8 tests passed (includes a browser test added while the full suite was running).
- 1,000 primary audit questions plus 250 confirmation calls: 500 direct/phrasing answers matched source quotations; all 250 known typo cases recovered after confirmation; all 250 unsupported cases refused.

Preserve existing greeting routes. Keep literals, negation, added conditions, and compound questions out of the new normalization. Compound handling retains the source question. Source follow-ups retain the selected subject and use the unchanged page eligibility, profile, provenance, and quotation checks. No random sampling, model, fuzzy entity matching, or promotion of chat to evidence.

Include executable per-class evaluation plus all 240 scenario records and source hashes under evaluation/conversation-repairs. pull_requests.title: Require supported answers; add constrained procedures and off-record chat
pull_requests.body:
Scope matching could return a page about the wrong entity, and bare-topic inspection could appear to be an answer. This separates those contracts while preserving the archived engine and source pins.

Changes:
- Installed CLI and normal UI Ask use the separately packaged supported-answer layer. Explicit candidates mode retains legacy inspection; old Python API/module remain unchanged for reproduction.
- Shared finite question frames normalize paraphrases, preserve subject identity, and check eligible body evidence and conflicts.
- Source-authored linear procedure tags preserve order, prerequisites, conditions, warnings and exact provenance. Fully explicit numbered procedures are automatically tagged; incomplete drafts cannot support generation. Context never proves completion.
- A final response guard rechecks procedural rendering, supported statements, grounded attributes, relation proofs and source pins.
- Off-the-record free chat is deterministic, explicitly not source-backed, and held in memory only. Chat messages cannot fetch/import sources or save/export/resume a transcript. Synthetic comparison tooling is included.

Evidence and limitations:
- Main was verified at 715d1b5. All 237 protected core/resource/capture/frozen-benchmark files remain byte-identical.
- Full follow-up regression run: 574 tests pass. Two subsequently added automatic-tag tests pass in the final 21-test procedure/reliability run; current main-test inventory is 576. Earlier 351 vendored tests passed on the unchanged components.
- UI-script, browser-transport, crawler fixtures and actual WebAssembly checks pass, including ephemeral-mode isolation. Latest bundled automatic tagging/rendering also passes.
- Development evaluation improves from 21/28 to 28/28 versus prior supported answering (8/8 answerable coverage, zero wrong returns, three correct ambiguities).
- The four frozen legacy wrong returns are refused by supported answering. Frozen pottery answer coverage remains ZERO; untagged procedural prose has not been solved. All 19 legacy non-correct cases are individually diagnosed without relabeling.
- External 20-question SQuAD sample: zero answers, ten false refusals, ten correct refusals; precision is undefined and answerable coverage is zero. Regression success is not general accuracy.
- Live baseline layout, reload persistence and source inspection were checked. Updated rendered layout and live deployed crawler are still unverified; fixture results are separate.

See docs/ANSWER_RELIABILITY.md and docs/PROCEDURAL_CONSTRAINTS.md for results, migration, source format, privacy scope and rollback. Hashes prove consistency, not truth; finite grammar does not establish general language understanding. No main merge or deployment is included.

pull_requests.title: Add window.MPLPB API for local use and optional online AI middleware
pull_requests.body:
People and browser-capable AI agents need a direct way to use MPLPB's existing engine without operating UI controls.

This adds window.MPLPB v1.0.0 for strict queries, corpus/page inspection, local chat, saved transcripts and supplied-text imports. Responses retain the engine's decisions, citations, delivery rules and provenance. Calls are asynchronous and use the existing browser worker or desktop transport.

Network access is off by default. Each chat call can explicitly opt into Wikipedia acquisition with allowNetwork:true; the standalone browser also supports autoWiki:true. Subsequent calls return to local-only behavior unless explicitly enabled again. No hosted MPLPB API service or API key is required. The README and JAVASCRIPT-API.md explain fully offline operation, AI frontend/middleware integration, optional internet acquisition, and the separate requirements of a cloud AI or hosted general-web crawler.

Also ensures future API calls fail promptly after a worker crash, and retains compatibility with the prior browser capture adapter because acquisition semantics are unchanged.

Validation completed:
- Public JavaScript API against the real Python bridge, including offline denial, opt-in synthetic Wikipedia captures, local follow-ups, ambiguity/refusal, profile enforcement, imports, sessions and invalid inputs.
- All 618 Python regression tests passed (236 seconds), including browser bridge and desktop UI tests.
- Existing UI script and browser transport checks.
- Standalone build with the pinned Pyodide release; complete existing WebAssembly checks plus public API checks.
- git diff --check.

Online tests use synthetic source responses, not a live Wikipedia availability check. No graphical-browser layout or real IndexedDB smoke test was run.

This draft does not merge or deploy the change.
